D000268.s: A property of the surface of an object that makes it stick to another surface.

D000794.s: A vascular, horny neoplasm of the skin characterized by telangiectasis and secondary epithelial changes including acanthosis and hyperkeratosis.

D000871.s: Agents that kill parasitic worms. They are used therapeutically in the treatment of helminthiasis in man and animal.

D003254.s: The promotion and support of consumers' rights and interests.

D005414.s: Production or presence of gas in the gastrointestinal tract which may be expelled through the anus.

D006961.s: A condition of abnormally elevated output of parathyroid hormone (or PTH) triggering responses that increase blood calcium. It is characterized by hypercalcemia and bone resorption, eventually leading to bone diseases.

D007131.s: Allelic variants of the kappa light chains (immunoglobulin kappa-chains) encoded by alleles of immunoglobulin light chain genes.

D010315.s: Devices which accelerate electrically charged atomic or subatomic particles, such as electrons, protons or ions, to high velocities so they have high kinetic energy.

D010360.s: Interfacility or intrahospital transfer of patients. Intrahospital transfer is usually to obtain a specific kind of care and interfacility transfer is usually for economic reasons as well as for the type of care provided.

D010816.s: Compensatory plans designed to motivate physicians in relation to patient referral, physician recruitment, and efficient use of the health facility.

D010979.s: Laboratory examination used to monitor and evaluate platelet function in a patient's blood.

D015576.s: Increase in the mass of bone per unit volume.

D015811.s: Tumors of the iris characterized by increased pigmentation of melanocytes. Malignant melanoma of the iris often originates from preexisting nevi.

D016106.s: Non-susceptibility of a microbe to the action of methicillin, a semi-synthetic penicillin derivative.

D016483.s: B-cell lymphoid tumors that occur in association with AIDS. Patients often present with an advanced stage of disease and highly malignant subtypes including burkitt lymphoma; immunoblastic large-cell lymphoma; primary effusion lymphoma; and diffuse, large B-cell, lymphoma.

D016609.s: Abnormal growths of tissue that follow a previous neoplasm but are not metastases of the latter. The second neoplasm may have the same or different histological type and can occur in the same or different organs as the previous neoplasm but in all cases arises from an independent oncogenic event.

D016717.s: Incision of sphincter of oddi or vater'S ampulla performed by inserting a sphincterotome through duodenoscope often following or performed during ERCP (endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography).

D017358.s: A mucoprotein found in the cell wall of various types of bacteria. It has adjuvant and antitumor activities and has been used to augment the production of lymphokine-activated killer (LAK) cells.

D017615.s: Two ganglionated neural plexuses in the gut wall which form one of the three major divisions of the autonomic nervous system. The enteric nervous system innervates the gastrointestinal tract, the pancreas, and the gallbladder. It contains sensory neurons, interneurons, and motor neurons.

D018023.s: Immune status consisting of non-production of HIV antibodies, as determined by various serological tests.

D020235.s: Impaired ambulation not attributed to sensory impairment or motor weakness. Frontal lobe disorders; basal ganglia diseases (e.g., parkinsonian disorders); dementia, multi-infarct; alzheimer disease; and other conditions may be associated with gait apraxia.

D020240.s: A form of apraxia characterized by an acquired inability to carry out a complex motor activity despite the ability to mentally formulate the action.

D020921.s: Sleep disorders characterized by impaired arousal from the deeper stages of sleep (generally stage III or IV sleep).

D029221.s: The use of faith and spirit to cure disease.

D042882.s: Solid crystalline precipitates in the biliary tract, usually formed in the gallbladder, resulting in the condition of cholelithiasis. Gallstones, derived from the BILE, consist mainly of calcium, cholesterol, or bilirubin.

D050153.s: Fatty tissue in the region of the abdomen. It includes the abdominal subcutaneous fat and the intra-abdominal fat.

D051381.s: The common name for the genus Rattus.

D052065.s: Recurrent or persistent involuntary spasm of the outer muscles of the vagina, occurring during vaginal penetration.

D054580.s: Component of the national institutes of health. D055877.s: Monitoring of information sources of potential value in detecting an emerging epidemic, whether naturally occurring or the result of bioterrorism.

D056667.s: A method of differentiating individuals based on the analysis of qualitative or quantitative biological traits or patterns.

D059208.s: Measure of the number of the parasites present in a host organism.

D061988.s: Compounds that inhibit the function or proteolytic action of the proteasome.

D065816.s: The nursing specialty focusing on the needs of patients with dysfunction of the nervous system.

D000066792.s: Dentists who specialize in the treatment of misaligned teeth and malocclusion.

D000068237.s: Counseling conducted via electronic or other non-face-to-face interactions.

D000078922.s: Lists of books and other information sources held among a cooperating group of libraries.

D000090362.s: A spectrum of primary, secondary, and idiopathic disorders involving mast cells and characterized by an aberrant release of mast cell mediators which result in multiple and variable inflammatory and allergic symptoms.

D000092225.s: Mycobacterium infections of organs other than the lung.
